saints.name: St. Louis Marie de Montfort
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: A tireless missionary of the poor whose “True Devotion” shaped modern Marian piety…
biography: Born at Montfort in Brittany on 31 January 1673, Louis-Marie Grignion studied with the Jesuits at Rennes and walked to Paris at nineteen for his theology, giving away his money and vowing to live on alms. Ordained in 1700, he found his vocation in 1705 as a preacher of parish missions.

For seventeen years he walked the villages of Brittany and the Vendée, preaching with fire, reviving the Rosary, and raising with his people's hands a monumental calvary at Pontchâteau that the government, stirred by Jansenist intrigue, ordered demolished. Poisoned once at La Rochelle, he never fully recovered his health.

He founded the Daughters of Wisdom at Poitiers in 1703 for the care of the sick poor and the Company of Mary in 1713 for missionary priests, and in his Treatise on True Devotion to the Blessed Virgin he taught total consecration to Jesus through Mary, a teaching that has shaped Catholic devotion ever since.

Worn out by his labours, he died at Saint-Laurent-sur-Sèvre on 28 April 1716, aged forty-three, leaving his two congregations only a handful of members. He was beatified by Leo XIII in 1888 and canonized by Pius XII in 1947.
saints.knownFor: His missions to the poor and his teaching on consecration to Christ through Mary.

sources.text: Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), “Blessed Louis-Marie Grignion de Montfort”
